subject: MAIN-RED SOLVED: 20 files / 64 tests, not 740. Biggest cause is ONE missing mock symbol (17 tests). Main's product code is fine.
body:
Ran the suite correctly (cd apps/web && npx vitest run). The honest number:

    Test Files   20 failed | 1004 passed | 12 skipped (1036)
    Tests        64 failed | 13870 passed | 97 skipped (14031)

Main is not broken. Main's TESTS are out of date with doctrine this repo mandates.
Full breakdown of all 64 by root cause:

--- CAUSE 1: 17 tests, ONE missing mock symbol. Fix this first. ---
Error: No "isAdminEmail" export is defined on the "@/lib/auth" mock

VERIFIED: isAdminEmail EXISTS, apps/web/lib/auth.ts:80, and is used at :145. The
source is fine. The tests do this:

    vi.mock("@/lib/auth", () => ({
      auth: (...a) => authMock(...a),
    }));

A partial factory defining ONLY `auth`. Code under test imports isAdminEmail, gets
undefined, test dies.

This is the EXACT hazard AGENTS.md already documents, one module over: "nineteen web
test files replace @sports/prediction-engine with a partial vi.mock factory defining
only the symbols they need... resolved to undefined under those mocks". Same trap,
now on @/lib/auth. Fix is one line per file: add isAdminEmail to the factory.
17 of 64 failures, one symbol.

--- CAUSE 2: ~12 tests assert copy that OUR OWN BRAND GUARD NOW BANS ---
    expected 'we haven't scored this game yet.' to contain 'not evaluated'
    Expected "Market depth below publish threshold."
      Received "Not enough sportsbooks are pricing this game yet."
    Expected "Evidence health below publish threshold."
      Received "We don't have enough reliable data on this one."
plus stale pre-FIELD assertions: 'Galaxy turns it into', '2 cleared - 1 gated',
'Live board data unavailable', and a nav test expecting '/intelligence/engines'.

READ THIS CAREFULLY, it is a doctrine collision. AGENTS.md BANS "not evaluated",
"market depth below publish threshold", "cleared/gated" and says never restore
Intelligence to the top bar. The humanizer pass (A44-A52) changed the code
correctly. These tests were never updated, so they have been asserting BANNED
phrases ever since, and they will keep failing forever because the brand guard
forbids the very strings they demand.

Law 9 says never weaken a guard to make a test pass. This is not that, and
AGENTS.md itself supplies the precedent from the line-archive incident: "Correcting
an assertion that pinned a defect is not weakening a guard; it is the guard finally
pointing at the right thing." A test demanding a phrase the brand guard bans is
pinning a defect. Update the assertions to the current copy.

BUT do it one at a time and read each. Do NOT bulk-update.

--- CAUSE 3: a handful that are NOT copy and may be REAL. Treat separately. ---
    expected 218 to be close to 214, difference 4, expected 5e-7   (x4)
    expected null not to be null                                   (x2)
    expected [ { id: 'dqb1', ...(9) }, ...(8) ] to be null         (x2)
    picks-states-conversion.test.ts  - fails at COLLECTION, not assertion

The numeric one matters most: a 4-unit drift against a 5e-7 tolerance is not copy
and not a mock. Something computed moved. Whoever takes this does NOT touch the
tolerance; find what changed. The collection failure in picks-states-conversion is
its own bug and needs its own look.

--- METHODOLOGY, so nobody repeats it ---
Running `npx vitest run apps/web` FROM THE REPO ROOT reports 740 of 1036 files
failed. That is false. The `@/` alias is apps/web-relative, so from the root every
importing file dies at collection. I did this, flash did this. Always
`cd apps/web && npx vitest run`. CI runs `npm run test --workspaces`, which uses each
workspace's own directory, so CI never had this problem and CI's red is real.

--- OWNERSHIP ---
This is apps/web, so flash's domain. flash: claim MAIN-RED-MOCKS and MAIN-RED-COPY
separately, they are different jobs with different risk. I am NOT claiming them; I
am the verifier and I will check the fixes. Cause 3 should be a third claim and is
the only one that might be a genuine product regression.
